assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
subdomain scope is program-aided math (PAL/PoT), CAS-exact computation (SymPy), strict numeric output schema, and answer verification
evaluation is exact-match centric (or tolerance-bounded numeric equality) on math benchmarks
code execution via sandboxed Python interpreter is the primary computation mechanism
exclusions: neural arithmetic units and differentiable programming
training data generation beyond (problem, code, answer) triple curation
model serving infrastructure and GPU optimization
multi-modal math (diagram understanding, geometry image parsing)

competency_questions.question: How does the PAL framework prevent LLM arithmetic hallucination?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PAL_FRAMEWORK node defines delegation of computation to Python interpreter

competency_questions.question: What is the difference between PAL and PoT and when should each be used?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PAL_FRAMEWORK and POT_FRAMEWORK distinguish code-only vs annotated approaches

competency_questions.question: When should SymPy CAS be used instead of Python numeric arithmetic?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SYMPY_CAS and TOOL_SELECTION define routing policy for exact vs approximate

competency_questions.question: How is the strict numeric output schema enforced to prevent free-text number hallucination?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STRICT_OUTPUT_SCHEMA and HALLUCINATION_GUARD define enforcement mechanism

competency_questions.question: How does the system extract, normalize, and validate the final numeric answer from code execution?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NUMERIC_OUTPUT_SCHEMA defines pipeline from stdout to canonical answer

competency_questions.question: What numeric precision and tolerance policy prevents false failures from floating-point representation?
How are units validated to catch dimensionally-wrong answers?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: UNIT_FORMAT_VALIDATOR defines unit ontology and validation

competency_questions.question: How does the system recover from code execution failures?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CODE_ERROR_RECOVERY defines retry strategy with error reflection

competency_questions.question: How is answer correctness verified beyond schema compliance?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ANSWER_VERIFIER defines back-substitution and self-consistency methods

competency_questions.question: How does the regression suite guard against regressions from system updates?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REGRESSION_SUITE defines versioned fixture bank and coverage policy

competency_questions.question: How is benchmark contamination detected and what happens when it is found?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GOODHART_RISK defines contamination detection and remediation

competency_questions.question: How are training datasets curated to ensure program-answer pair quality?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DATASET_CURATION defines curation pipeline with human verification

competency_questions.question: What security controls prevent LLM-generated code from causing harm in production?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SANDBOX_EXECUTOR defines import allowlist and resource limits

competency_questions.question: How is the latency-cost-accuracy tradeoff managed for production deployment?

glossary.definition: Program-Aided Language Models; LLM generates Python code to compute math answers
Program of Thoughts; interleaved reasoning comments and executable Python code
Python library for exact symbolic mathematics and computer algebra
Machine-parseable format specification requiring numeric answer with unit and format; no prose
Sampling N code solutions and taking majority vote on the extracted numeric answer
Plugging computed answer back into original equation to verify it satisfies the constraint
Overfitting to benchmark metrics through contamination or optimization pressure; benchmark score diverges from true capability
Isolated execution environment with resource limits, import allowlist, and no filesystem/network access for running LLM-generated code
Acceptable difference between computed and reference numeric answer for comparison purposes

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for tool-grounded math reasoning work units in absence of supplied datasets; informed by PAL (Gao et al. 2022) and PoT (Chen et al. 2022) papers
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Gao et al. 2022 (PAL: Program-aided Language Models); Chen et al. 2022 (Program of Thoughts Prompting)
grounding_limits: domain-general heuristic priors informed by PAL/PoT literature

nodes.definition: Implement the PAL paradigm: LLM generates Python code to solve math tasks; Python interpreter executes for exact numeric output; LLM never does arithmetic itself.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: switch to non-Python CAS or model generates non-executable output

pros.claim: Eliminates arithmetic hallucination by delegating computation to a deterministic interpreter
pros.example: PAL on GSM8K outperforms chain-of-thought by delegating arithmetic to Python

cons.claim: Requires sandboxed code execution environment; adds latency and infra complexity
cons.example: Docker sandbox adds ~200ms per query

failure_modes: LLM generates syntactically invalid Python
interpreter timeout on infinite loops
import of disallowed modules
acceptance_tests: generated code executes without exception on fixture problems
numeric output matches reference answer within tolerance
revisit_triggers: problem class shifts to require non-Python libraries

nodes.definition: Implement the PoT variant (Chen et al. 2022): LLM generates multi-step chain of computations as code comments interleaved with executable Python, separating reasoning steps from computation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: reasoning annotation style changes or PoT template updated

pros.claim: Step-level comments make reasoning auditable and error-localizable
pros.example: comment per step lets reviewers spot where reasoning diverged from computation

cons.claim: Longer prompts increase cost and may exceed context window on complex problems
cons.example: multi-step annotation can use 3× tokens vs. PAL

failure_modes: comments diverge from actual computation path
step order inconsistencies
acceptance_tests: each reasoning step maps to a corresponding code block
final variable matches expected output
revisit_triggers: model starts condensing steps to save tokens

nodes.definition: Integrate SymPy as the computation backend for exact symbolic and algebraic operations: solve equations, simplify expressions, compute limits/derivatives, and avoid floating-point rounding.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: SymPy version upgrade or switch to alternative CAS

pros.claim: Exact rational arithmetic eliminates floating-point accumulation errors
pros.example: SymPy gives Rational(1,3) not 0.3333...

cons.claim: SymPy solve() can time out on large polynomial systems; not all problems are symbolically tractable
cons.example: groebner basis on degree-8 polynomial hangs >30s

failure_modes: LLM imports numpy instead of sympy for symbolic tasks
SymPy timeout on underdetermined systems
acceptance_tests: SymPy-generated answer matches exact reference on 10 algebraic fixtures
no floating-point equality checks used when exact answer required
revisit_triggers: problem shifts to numerical ODE integration where SymPy is too slow

nodes.definition: Define and enforce a machine-parseable output schema for numeric answers: single number, unit, format (integer/decimal/fraction), no prose explanation appended. All tool-math responses must conform.

included: integer vs decimal vs fraction policy

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new answer type (complex, vector) added to problem corpus

pros.claim: Machine-parseable schema enables automated answer checking without NLP extraction
pros.example: regex match on structured output gives 100% parse rate vs ~85% on free-text

cons.claim: Overly strict schema breaks on legitimate edge cases (complex numbers, vectors, sets)
cons.example: schema requiring float fails on set-valued answers like {1,2,3}

failure_modes: schema too narrow for problem class
unit ambiguity when problem omits units
precision format mismatch
acceptance_tests: all fixture answers pass schema validation
schema rejects known-bad formats without false negatives
revisit_triggers: new problem domain with non-scalar answers introduced

nodes.definition: Extract the final numeric answer from code stdout or variable, normalize to canonical form (e.g., simplify fractions, strip trailing zeros, apply unit), and validate against schema before emitting.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: normalization rules revised or new problem domains onboarded

pros.claim: Normalization decouples format representation from correctness check
pros.example: 0.5 and 1/2 both normalize to same canonical before comparison

cons.claim: Normalization rules must cover all edge cases or silently corrupt answer
cons.example: 0.10 incorrectly stripped to 0.1 causing unit mismatch

failure_modes: trailing-zero stripping changes answer precision
fraction to decimal loss of exactness
unit not applied before comparison
acceptance_tests: normalized form of known fixture answers matches reference canonical
extraction raises explicit error rather than returning None
revisit_triggers: new problem domain adds new unit classes

nodes.definition: Verify the extracted numeric answer using independent checks: back-substitution into equation, re-execution with different code path, or majority vote across N sampled code generations.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new problem class where back-substitution is ill-defined

pros.claim: Back-substitution catches errors that normalization cannot (wrong equation)
pros.example: plug x=3 back into 2x+1=7: 7=7 confirms answer

cons.claim: Self-consistency voting at N=5 multiplies inference cost 5×; expensive at scale
cons.example: N=5 samples costs 5× API fee per query

failure_modes: majority vote masks systematic bias if all generations share same wrong assumption
back-substitution only checks algebraic consistency, not problem formulation correctness
acceptance_tests: verifier catches known-wrong answer in fixture test bank
back-substitution passes for all correct fixture answers
revisit_triggers: problem class where back-substitution is undecidable

nodes.definition: Enforce a no-free-text numeric mode: LLM output must contain only code and/or a structured answer token; any prose numeric claim outside schema is rejected as potential hallucination.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: output schema revised to allow optional explanation field

pros.claim: Eliminates free-text numbers that cannot be reliably extracted or verified
pros.example: JSON-only mode gives 0% spurious number extraction

cons.claim: Strict mode prevents model from signaling uncertainty or special cases in natural language
cons.example: model cannot flag ambiguous problem statement

failure_modes: model finds loopholes (embeds number in variable name)
schema parser has regex that matches prose accidentally
acceptance_tests: no prose numeric values appear outside schema tags in 100% of fixture outputs
rejection log captures all schema violations
revisit_triggers: new output format allows optional commentary field

nodes.definition: Validate that the emitted answer carries the correct unit (SI, Imperial, dimensionless) and numeric format (integer, float with specified precision, fraction) required by the problem domain.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new unit classes added or precision requirements revised

pros.claim: Catches unit errors that are numerically correct but dimensionally wrong
pros.example: answer 9.8 kg rejected when problem asks for Newtons

cons.claim: Unit ontology must be maintained as problem domains expand
cons.example: adding financial units requires ontology update

failure_modes: unit omitted when required
imperial vs metric ambiguity
precision too coarse for problem
acceptance_tests: validator rejects known-wrong unit on 10 fixture cases
dimensionless problems pass without unit tag
revisit_triggers: new problem domain adds novel units

nodes.definition: Provide a secure, resource-limited code execution environment for LLM-generated Python: enforce import allowlist, CPU/memory/timeout limits, and prevent filesystem/network access.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: sandbox library updated or security policy changes

pros.claim: Prevents code injection, infinite loops, and data exfiltration from generated code
pros.example: allowlist blocks requests, os.system, subprocess

cons.claim: Sandbox startup overhead (~100-300ms) compounds with high query volume
cons.example: 10k queries/day × 200ms overhead = 33min extra wall-clock

failure_modes: sandbox escape via ctypes or cffi
timeout too short for legitimate complex computation
allowlist blocks needed math library
acceptance_tests: arbitrary code injection attempt fails safely
timeout fires correctly at configured limit
allowed SymPy operations complete within timeout
revisit_triggers: new library required by problem class is blocked

nodes.definition: Design few-shot prompt templates that reliably elicit syntactically correct, runnable Python code for math problems: format of examples, variable naming conventions, answer extraction comment.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: model upgrade requires re-calibrating few-shot examples

pros.claim: Well-engineered few-shot examples dramatically improve code syntactic correctness
pros.example: 5 curated examples raise parse success from 72% to 94%

cons.claim: Few-shot examples consume significant context tokens, reducing space for problem
cons.example: 5 examples at 150 tokens each = 750 token overhead per query

failure_modes: examples do not cover the problem's domain causing hallucinated libraries
answer variable name inconsistency breaks extractor
acceptance_tests: template produces syntactically valid Python on 95% of fixture problems
answer variable is consistently named per spec
revisit_triggers: new problem domain requires new examples beyond context window
model capability changes alter what examples are needed

nodes.definition: Evaluate tool-math system on standard benchmarks (GSM8K, MATH, SVAMP, ASDiv) using exact-match and normalized numeric equality; track per-category accuracy to identify failure modes.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: benchmark dataset updated or contamination discovered

pros.claim: Standardized benchmarks enable cross-system comparison and track progress
pros.example: GSM8K solve rate is de-facto PAL capability signal

cons.claim: Benchmark contamination inflates scores when training data overlaps with test split
cons.example: MATH test contamination inflates solve rate by estimated 5-15%

failure_modes: contamination inflating benchmark score
overfitting to benchmark format
category imbalance masking weaknesses
acceptance_tests: benchmark runner produces per-problem pass/fail log
contamination check run before reporting results

nodes.definition: Manage the risk that optimizing for specific math benchmarks leads to overfitting benchmark format/templates, contamination of test splits, and divergence between benchmark score and real-world utility.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new benchmark released or training data augmented with web content

pros.claim: Proactive contamination detection prevents inflated scores misleading stakeholders
pros.example: n-gram overlap check catches 89% of MATH test set contamination

cons.claim: Contamination detection is imperfect; semantic contamination evades n-gram checks
cons.example: rephrased problems still contaminate but evade overlap detector

failure_modes: semantic contamination undetected by surface overlap
goodhart pressure causes training data curation toward benchmark
acceptance_tests: contamination check runs before any public reporting
held-out private test set maintained separate from development
revisit_triggers: training data grows to include web-scraped math contests
benchmark data leaks through augmentation pipeline

nodes.definition: Handle code execution failures (SyntaxError, NameError, timeout) by: prompting LLM to self-correct with error message, retrying with simplified prompt, or falling back to direct chain-of-thought.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: production error rate changes or SLA tightens

pros.claim: Error reflection with error message enables LLM self-correction without human intervention
pros.example: showing TypeError message to LLM fixes ~60% of type errors on retry

cons.claim: Retry loop multiplies latency and cost; unbounded retries unacceptable in production
cons.example: 3 retries × 2s execution = 6s+ per failed query

failure_modes: infinite retry loop on deterministic error
CoT fallback produces free-text number violating schema
acceptance_tests: retry budget enforced; system returns error after N attempts
CoT fallback output still passes schema validation
revisit_triggers: error taxonomy expands with new execution environments
retry budget revised based on latency SLA

nodes.definition: Quantify and optimize the tradeoff: PAL adds interpreter latency; SymPy adds CAS time; N-sample voting multiplies cost; sandbox overhead is fixed. Choose operating point for production SLA.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: production traffic profile or pricing model changes

pros.claim: Explicit operating-point analysis prevents runaway costs from over-engineering accuracy
pros.example: N=3 vs N=1 gains 2% accuracy for 3× cost; N=1 chosen for SLA

cons.claim: Tradeoff curve is problem-distribution-dependent; operating point may not generalize
cons.example: optimal N on GSM8K may differ from production query mix

failure_modes: ignoring sandbox startup in latency budget
assuming homogeneous problem difficulty
acceptance_tests: latency budget allocation validated against production percentile targets
cost model shows P95 query cost within budget

nodes.definition: Decompose complex multi-step math problems into subproblems; route each to appropriate solver (PAL Python, SymPy CAS, direct arithmetic); recombine subresults into final answer.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new problem class requires new solver type

pros.claim: Decomposition allows each subproblem to use the best solver, improving accuracy on compound problems
pros.example: geometry sub + algebra sub each routed to SymPy; combined answer 8% more accurate

cons.claim: Decomposition errors propagate: wrong subproblem split causes incorrect final answer
cons.example: splitting 'total cost with tax' before computing tax base introduces error

failure_modes: incorrect decomposition splits an atomic step
circular dependency between subproblems
subresult unit mismatch on composition
acceptance_tests: composed answer matches direct-solve reference on 10 multi-step fixtures
dependency graph of subproblems is acyclic
revisit_triggers: problem class requires interleaved symbolic/numeric solving not captured by routing rules

nodes.definition: Specify and enforce numeric comparison tolerances: exact integer match, absolute tolerance for floats, relative tolerance for large numbers; prevent false failures from floating-point representation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: problem domain introduces new numeric representation requirements

pros.claim: Tolerance policy prevents false negatives from floating-point representation differences
pros.example: 1.4999999 and 1.5 compare equal under atol=1e-6

cons.claim: Tolerance too large masks genuine errors near the boundary
cons.example: atol=0.01 treats 9.99 as equal to 10.0 in a precision-sensitive context

failure_modes: tolerance too loose accepting wrong answers
tolerance applied to exact integer problems causing false passes
relative tolerance undefined for zero denominator
acceptance_tests: tolerance configuration reviewed for each answer type class
edge cases (zero, infinity, negative) covered in fixture set
revisit_triggers: SymPy exact answer compared with float answer requires policy

nodes.definition: Decide per-problem or per-problem-class which computation tool to invoke: direct LLM arithmetic (tiny/trivial), Python interpreter (procedural/numeric), SymPy CAS (symbolic/algebraic), external API (domain-specific).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: tool capability changes or problem taxonomy updated

pros.claim: Routing trivial arithmetic to direct LLM avoids sandbox overhead for simple cases
pros.example: 2+2=4 answered directly; SymPy reserved for 3x²+2x-8=0

cons.claim: Routing errors send symbolic problems to numeric solver causing precision loss
cons.example: routing algebra to numpy float instead of SymPy loses exactness

failure_modes: problem misclassified as simpler than it is
classifier latency exceeds savings from routing
acceptance_tests: routing correctly directs 95% of fixture problems to appropriate tool
misrouted problems are flagged rather than silently wrong

nodes.definition: Curate and augment training/evaluation datasets of math problems with (problem, program, answer) triples; ensure diversity across categories, difficulty levels, and avoid benchmark contamination.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: benchmark dataset updated or annotation error rate changes

pros.claim: Curated (problem, program, answer) triples with verified execution enable reliable supervised fine-tuning
pros.example: GSM8K-like triples with verified Python programs yield SFT gains of 8-15%

cons.claim: Manual curation is expensive; automated generation risks including incorrect programs
cons.example: auto-generated programs have ~15% error rate requiring human verification

failure_modes: incorrect program-answer pairs in training data
category imbalance over-representing easy problems
contamination from benchmark sources
acceptance_tests: random sample of 100 curated triples verified by human
decontamination overlap check passes before dataset frozen
revisit_triggers: annotator error rate increases with difficulty

nodes.definition: Fine-tune a base LLM on (problem, Python-solution, answer) triples to improve code generation quality, syntactic correctness, and domain-specific variable naming for math tool-use.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: base model updated or dataset distribution shifts significantly

pros.claim: Fine-tuning on verified programs dramatically improves code syntax correctness from base model
pros.example: SFT on 50k PAL triples raises parse success from 72% to 96%

cons.claim: Fine-tuning is expensive, tied to a base model version, and may degrade general reasoning
cons.example: LoRA fine-tune costs $200-$2000 GPU-hours; base model upgrade requires re-fine-tuning

failure_modes: catastrophic forgetting of general math reasoning
overfitting to training problem distribution
base model license restrictions on fine-tuned derivatives
acceptance_tests: fine-tuned model improves on held-out benchmark vs base model
fine-tuned model does not regress on general math fixtures

nodes.definition: Maintain a versioned regression test suite of math problems with expected answers, covering all problem types, edge cases (zero, negative, fraction, very large numbers), and schema validation checks.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: system component updated or new problem types onboarded

pros.claim: Regression suite catches regressions from model updates, schema changes, and library upgrades
pros.example: regression run caught SymPy API break in 23/50 tests after version upgrade

cons.claim: Maintaining regression fixtures is ongoing effort; stale fixtures give false confidence
cons.example: fixtures not updated for new problem types create blind spots

failure_modes: stale fixtures not covering new problem types
flaky tests from floating-point non-determinism
regression masking by overfitting to fixture set
acceptance_tests: regression suite runs in CI with <5min execution time
100% of high-risk schema paths covered by at least one fixture
revisit_triggers: new problem types added to system

nodes.definition: Monitor production tool-math pipeline for answer distribution drift, error rate changes, latency degradation, and sandbox failure rates; alert and trigger re-evaluation when thresholds crossed.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: production traffic characteristics change or SLA revised

pros.claim: Real-time monitoring catches distribution shifts that offline benchmarks miss
pros.example: error spike from new problem type detected 4h after deployment

cons.claim: Production monitoring requires logging infrastructure and may log sensitive problem data
cons.example: logging math problems may expose user data in regulated domains

failure_modes: drift goes undetected until significant accuracy drop
alert thresholds too sensitive causing alert fatigue
acceptance_tests: alert fires within 1h of simulated error rate spike in staging
latency P95 tracked and compared against SLA

edges.resolution_rule: latency budget limits N for voting; must be negotiated explicitly
if contamination confirmed, benchmark results must be invalidated and re-run on clean split
CoT fallback in error recovery must still pass hallucination guard schema check
SymPy exact computation can exceed latency budget; use timeout with fallback

conflict_axes.name: exact_vs_approximate
conflict_axes.description: SymPy exact arithmetic vs numpy float approximation; exact is correct but slower and may timeout for large problems
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: default to SymPy; fall back to numpy only when CAS timeout documented

conflict_axes.name: accuracy_vs_latency
conflict_axes.description: N-sample self-consistency voting improves accuracy but multiplies latency and cost linearly
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: set N by SLA budget; expose N as configurable parameter not hardcoded

conflict_axes.name: strict_schema_vs_expressiveness
conflict_axes.description: no-free-text mode eliminates hallucination but prevents model from signaling uncertainty or edge cases
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: add optional structured uncertainty flag to schema without prose numbers

conflict_axes.name: benchmark_optimization_vs_goodhart
conflict_axes.description: optimizing for benchmark scores incentivizes contamination and overfitting to benchmark formats
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold out private test set; measure on OOD problems before claiming benchmark SOTA

conflict_axes.name: sandbox_security_vs_expressiveness
conflict_axes.description: strict import allowlist prevents code injection but may block legitimate math libraries needed for novel problem types
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: maintain allowlist per problem domain; expand with security review process

conflict_axes.name: fine_tuning_cost_vs_generality
conflict_axes.description: fine-tuning on PAL triples improves task accuracy but is expensive, tied to base model, and may degrade general reasoning
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use LoRA/PEFT to limit forgetting; gate fine-tuning on ROI analysis

conflict_axes.name: pal_vs_pot_verbosity
conflict_axes.description: PoT's annotated reasoning is more auditable but uses significantly more tokens than PAL's code-only approach
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use PAL for production latency-sensitive paths; PoT for debugging and audit trails

conflict_axes.name: decomposition_accuracy_vs_error_propagation
conflict_axes.description: problem decomposition improves handling of complex problems but introduces error propagation risk from subproblem misidentification
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: verify each subresult before composition; flag decomposition failures explicitly

conflict_axes.name: dataset_curation_cost_vs_quality
conflict_axes.description: high-quality curated (problem, program, answer) triples require expensive human verification but automated curation has high error rate
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use automated generation with selective human verification on high-difficulty examples

conflict_axes.name: tolerance_strictness_vs_false_failures
conflict_axes.description: strict exact-match comparison prevents false passes but causes false failures from float representation; tolerance too loose allows wrong answers near boundary
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use exact match for integer answers; configure per-domain tolerance for floats

edge_cases.description: SymPy times out on large polynomial system (degree >= 7)
edge_cases.mitigation: set per-call SymPy timeout; fall back to numerical solver with explicit precision warning

edge_cases.description: LLM generates Python that imports disallowed module (requests, os)
edge_cases.mitigation: sandbox blocks import; error recovery reprompts with allowlist hint

edge_cases.description: Problem requires set-valued or interval answer incompatible with scalar schema
edge_cases.mitigation: extend schema with set/interval types for relevant problem classes before deployment

edge_cases.description: Self-consistency voting majority is wrong due to shared systematic bias in generated code
edge_cases.mitigation: include diversity-promoting sampling temperature variation; validate majority against back-substitution

edge_cases.description: Benchmark test split contaminated in training data
edge_cases.mitigation: run n-gram and semantic decontamination before training; maintain private hold-out

edge_cases.description: Unit ambiguity: problem states 'weight' without specifying kg vs lbs
edge_cases.mitigation: schema requires problem pre-processor to resolve unit ambiguity before code generation

edge_cases.description: Very large integer (>10^18) causes overflow in Python int or numpy but not SymPy
edge_cases.mitigation: route large-integer problems to SymPy; block numpy int64 for such problems

edge_cases.description: Retry loop on SyntaxError becomes infinite when LLM regenerates same broken code
edge_cases.mitigation: hash previous attempts; refuse to retry identical code; escalate to CoT fallback

edge_cases.description: Fine-tuned model overfits to training distribution, failing OOD math problem types
edge_cases.mitigation: include OOD problem types in validation set; use early stopping on OOD validation loss

edge_cases.description: Problem decomposer creates circular dependency between subproblems
edge_cases.mitigation: validate subproblem dependency graph is DAG before execution; raise explicit error on cycle

edge_cases.description: Floating-point comparison at tolerance boundary causes non-deterministic test results
edge_cases.mitigation: use exact rational arithmetic for boundary cases; document all tolerance values explicitly

edge_cases.description: Production query distribution shifts (new problem type) causing silent accuracy drop
edge_cases.mitigation: monitor answer distribution entropy and error rate; alert on statistical drift

workflow.description: Specify strict numeric output schema and unit conventions before any code generation or evaluation
workflow.gate: schema validated against known answer types

workflow.description: Configure sandboxed Python execution environment with import allowlist, resource limits, timeout policy
workflow.gate: sandbox blocks known-bad code and allows known-good code

workflow.description: Design and validate PAL/PoT few-shot prompt templates for target problem domains
workflow.gate: templates produce syntactically valid Python on 95% of fixture problems

workflow.description: Integrate SymPy as exact computation backend; configure timeout and fallback to numeric where appropriate
workflow.gate: SymPy produces exact answers for algebraic fixture set within timeout

workflow.description: Implement extraction, normalization, tolerance check, unit validation, and schema compliance pipeline
workflow.gate: all fixture answers extracted and validated without false pass/fail

workflow.description: Implement answer verification (back-substitution, self-consistency voting) with configurable N and retry budget
workflow.gate: verifier catches all known-wrong answers in fixture bank

workflow.description: Curate (problem, program, answer) training triples with decontamination check and human verification sample
workflow.gate: random 100-sample human review passes; decontamination check passes

workflow.description: Fine-tune base LLM on curated PAL triples using PEFT/LoRA; validate on held-out benchmark
workflow.gate: fine-tuned model improves on held-out benchmark without regressing on general math

workflow.description: Implement problem decomposition and tool selection routing for complex multi-step problems
workflow.gate: routing correctly directs 95% of fixtures; decomposer produces DAG subproblems

workflow.description: Evaluate complete pipeline on GSM8K, MATH, SVAMP benchmarks; run Goodhart contamination check first
workflow.gate: contamination check passes before results published

workflow.description: Build and run regression test suite covering all schema paths, edge cases, and problem categories
workflow.gate: 100% of high-risk schema paths covered; suite runs in <5min

workflow.description: Deploy to production with latency/cost operating point set; configure drift detection and alerting
workflow.gate: staging stress test passes SLA; drift detection fires on simulated spike

dominance_rules.rule: PAL_FRAMEWORK dominates free-text numeric generation for all math tasks requiring multi-step computation
dominance_rules.condition: task involves arithmetic, algebra, or calculus with more than 1 computation step
dominance_rules.rationale: delegation to Python interpreter eliminates arithmetic hallucination

dominance_rules.rule: SYMPY_CAS dominates numpy for algebraic and symbolic problems
dominance_rules.condition: problem requires exact rational arithmetic, symbolic algebra, or equation solving
dominance_rules.rationale: SymPy provides exact answers avoiding floating-point accumulation

dominance_rules.rule: STRICT_OUTPUT_SCHEMA dominates all output formatting decisions
dominance_rules.condition: any numeric answer is being emitted to downstream consumer
dominance_rules.rationale: schema compliance is prerequisite for automated answer checking

dominance_rules.rule: HALLUCINATION_GUARD dominates when prose numeric values are detected
dominance_rules.condition: any prose numeric value appears outside schema-designated fields
dominance_rules.rationale: prose number extraction has unacceptably high error rate vs schema-structured output

dominance_rules.rule: SANDBOX_EXECUTOR dominates when any untrusted LLM-generated code is executed
dominance_rules.condition: code was generated by LLM rather than authored by human engineer
dominance_rules.rationale: LLM-generated code must be treated as untrusted input regardless of apparent safety

dominance_rules.rule: GOODHART_RISK check dominates before publishing any benchmark results
dominance_rules.condition: benchmark evaluation results are being reported externally or used for model selection
dominance_rules.rationale: contaminated benchmark results cause incorrect model selection decisions

dominance_rules.rule: ANSWER_VERIFIER dominates single-shot answer acceptance for high-stakes problems
dominance_rules.condition: problem is high-stakes (financial, medical, engineering) or answer is flagged as uncertain
dominance_rules.rationale: back-substitution provides independent correctness signal beyond schema compliance

dominance_rules.rule: PRECISION_TOLERANCE policy dominates equality checks between numeric values
dominance_rules.condition: any two numeric values are being compared for equality in answer checking
dominance_rules.rationale: raw float equality causes false failures from representation differences

dominance_rules.rule: DATASET_CURATION decontamination dominates before any fine-tuning run
dominance_rules.condition: training data includes any source that may overlap with benchmark test splits
dominance_rules.rationale: contaminated fine-tuning data causes benchmark score inflation masking real performance

dominance_rules.rule: REGRESSION_SUITE CI gate dominates before any code deployment
dominance_rules.condition: any component of the tool-math pipeline is being updated or replaced
dominance_rules.rationale: regression suite catches silent breakages faster and more comprehensively than manual review

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not re-implement arithmetic inside the LLM response; always delegate to Python
anti_rework_rules.trigger: anyone proposes LLM should compute arithmetic in text rather than code

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not change output schema after answer extraction pipeline is tested; schema changes require full regression re-run
anti_rework_rules.trigger: schema change proposed without triggering regression suite re-run

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not tune tolerance parameters without documenting which problem types they apply to
anti_rework_rules.trigger: global tolerance changed without per-type documentation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not expand sandbox import allowlist without security review
anti_rework_rules.trigger: new library requested for addition to allowlist

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not publish benchmark results before running Goodhart contamination check
anti_rework_rules.trigger: benchmark evaluation complete and results being prepared for sharing

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not fine-tune on a dataset that has not passed decontamination
Do not hard-code N for self-consistency voting; always expose as configurable parameter
Do not use raw Python equality (==) for float answer comparison; always use tolerance policy
anti_rework_rules.trigger: equality check is being written for numeric answer comparison

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not add prose explanation to model output without extending schema to structured optional field
anti_rework_rules.trigger: user requests explanation alongside numeric answer

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not deploy without staging regression suite passing; no manual exception process
Do not route symbolic algebra problems to numpy; always route to SymPy
anti_rework_rules.trigger: tool routing policy is being configured

iteration_protocol.name: schema_first
iteration_protocol.description: Output schema and unit convention must be finalized before any code generation or evaluation begins; no exceptions
iteration_protocol.trigger: starting a new math tool-math deployment or problem domain
iteration_protocol.action: run WF_01 (schema definition) to completion with human sign-off
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: schema spec reviewed and accepted_tests defined

iteration_protocol.name: sandbox_before_execution
iteration_protocol.description: Sandbox configuration must be validated before any LLM-generated code is executed, even in development
iteration_protocol.trigger: new execution environment or sandbox policy change
iteration_protocol.action: run sandbox smoke tests against allowlist and blocklist
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: allowlist and blocklist both verified by security review

iteration_protocol.name: contamination_check_before_train
iteration_protocol.description: Run decontamination check before every fine-tuning run regardless of assumed data provenance
iteration_protocol.trigger: new training dataset version or augmentation applied
iteration_protocol.action: run n-gram and semantic overlap check against all benchmark test splits
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: contamination report shows <1% overlap with any test split

iteration_protocol.name: regression_before_deploy
iteration_protocol.description: Full regression suite must pass before any component deployment; failing suite blocks deployment
iteration_protocol.trigger: any code change to any pipeline component
iteration_protocol.action: run complete regression suite including schema, edge cases, and category tests
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: regression suite passes with zero regressions

iteration_protocol.name: tolerance_review_on_domain_change
iteration_protocol.description: Precision tolerance policy must be reviewed whenever a new problem domain is added
iteration_protocol.action: enumerate answer types in new domain; update tolerance config per type
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: new domain's answer types all covered by tolerance policy

iteration_protocol.name: benchmark_contamination_gate
iteration_protocol.description: Contamination check must be run and passed before benchmark results are reported or used for model selection
iteration_protocol.action: run GOODHART_RISK contamination analysis; hold private test set comparison
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: contamination report clean; private test set confirms benchmark result

iteration_protocol.name: latency_cost_review_on_n_change
iteration_protocol.description: Operating point (N for voting, retry budget) must be re-validated against SLA when changed
iteration_protocol.action: run latency profiling in staging at new N; compare cost model
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: P95 latency within SLA budget at new N

iteration_protocol.name: tool_routing_update_on_new_domain
iteration_protocol.description: Tool selection routing policy must be updated when new problem domain or solver added
iteration_protocol.trigger: new problem type or computation tool added to system
iteration_protocol.action: update routing policy; add fixtures for new domain; verify routing on fixtures
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: routing achieves >=95% correct direction on new domain fixtures

iteration_protocol.name: production_drift_response
iteration_protocol.description: When production monitoring detects statistical drift, trigger offline benchmark re-evaluation and potential retraining
iteration_protocol.trigger: drift alert fired in production monitoring
iteration_protocol.action: run offline benchmark on production sample; compare to baseline; decide retrain or schema update
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: root cause identified and remediation plan approved

priority_rationale: Ordered by criticality and risk_if_wrong; PAL_FRAMEWORK and STRICT_OUTPUT_SCHEMA are foundational; HALLUCINATION_GUARD and SANDBOX_EXECUTOR are safety-critical; evaluation and governance nodes follow; operational and optimization nodes last.

structural_checks: edge ids unique in EDGE_NNN format
all edge from/to resolve to node ids
metric_checks: derived metrics set to 0 before formula tool run
ref_checks: all competency_question_refs resolve to competency_questions ids
all evidence_refs resolve to source_registry ids
all conflict_axis_refs resolve to conflict_axes ids
edge_checks: conflict edges have signed_tension<0 and resolution_rule
priority_checks: priority_order lists every node id exactly once

LLM attempts to embed numeric answer in prose
training data contains benchmark test problem
generated code attempts to import requests
